Consonantal i

SearchHow we decideRulings

Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

joke noun and verb

also jest, joking, tell a joke, make a joke, I was only joking, just kidding, kid, as a joke, joking apart

classical

Cic. Fam. 7.11.3: remōtō jocō tibi hoc amīcissimō animō praecipiō
Plaut. Poen. 541: equidem haec vōbīs dīxī per jocum

jocus, jocī m. (pl. joca)

noun, second declension; the plural joca is Cicero’s

a joke, jest

Per jocum or jocō, as a joke, in jest; the opposite is sēriō (see serious). Remōtō jocō and extrā jocum are “joking apart” (Lewis & Short). It also covers play and pastime generally (see fun).

Other words

  • jocor, jocārī, jocātus sum — joke, jest; say as a joke

    verb, first conjugation, deponent · classical · Cic. Fam. 9.14.4: haec enim jocātus sum; Ter. Heaut. 729b: Atquī tū hanc jocārī crēdis?

    Intransitive, or with what is said in jest: haec jocātus sum, I said this as a joke.

  • rīdiculum, rīdiculī n. — something laughable, a jest

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Quint. 6.3.22 (Lewis & Short); Cic. de Or. 2.235 (Lewis & Short)

    The laughable as a subject, as in Cicero’s and Quintilian’s chapters on wit; rīdiculī causā, for a laugh (Plaut. Am. 917). The adjective rīdiculus is funny, and also absurd (see funny).

Examples

  • Nimis īrācundī estis: equidem haec vōbīs dīxī per jocum.

    You’re far too touchy: I only said it as a joke.Plaut. Poen. 541

  • Heus tū, sī quid per jocum dīxī, nōlītō in sērium convertere.

    Hey, if I said something as a joke, don’t turn it into something serious.Plaut. Poen. 1320b–1321

  • extrā jocum homō bellus est

    joking apart, he’s a nice manCic. Fam. 7.16.2

  • Atquī tū hanc jocārī crēdis? Faciet, nisi caveō.

    And you think she’s joking? She’ll do it, unless I watch out.Ter. Heaut. 729b–730

See also fun, funny, serious, laugh.

SourcesLewis & Short: jocus · Lewis & Short: jocor · Lewis & Short: ridiculus
